claims.text: Replacing full thermodynamic integration with Local-Cluster Perturbation using an MTP will reduce computational cost by approximately an order of magnitude.
The proposed method will maintain sufficient accuracy for melting-point prediction in Ta-based BCC high-entropy alloys.
A liquid-structure-descriptor loss function will prevent the MTP from collapsing to the BCC crystal minimum during perturbation.
Standard EAM potentials fail to capture the disordered liquid structure of the Ta-based multicomponent alloy.
Ab initio thermodynamic integration is computationally prohibitive for the target alloy.
Localized nonequilibrium perturbations combined with Bennett Acceptance Ratio reweighting can replace the global thermodynamic-integration path.
The intervention forms transient icosahedral or distorted-polyhedral liquid-like clusters within the BCC lattice.
These transient liquid-like clusters act as nucleation seeds.
MTP tensorial descriptors accurately describe the proposed liquid-like local motifs.
EAM misses the proposed motifs because it relies on radial distribution information alone.
The relevant solid-liquid free-energy difference is dominated by local structural fluctuations.
Perturbing local clusters and reweighting their configurations bypasses the high-energy barriers associated with global phase transformations.
The local perturbation path can calculate the chemical-potential difference between the solid and liquid phases.
The predicted melting temperature will differ by less than 2% from high-fidelity ab initio benchmarks.
Computational time per data point will be reduced by a factor of 10–20 relative to standard DFT thermodynamic integration.
The method will predict suppression of the melting point due to configurational entropy in the multicomponent alloy.
The approach is applicable to refractory BCC high-entropy alloys with moderate to high atomic-size mismatch.
The approach may fail in systems with strong directional bonding or liquid chemical ordering absent from the training set.
Insufficient representation of multicomponent liquid environments can cause MTP extrapolation collapse, artificial solid stabilization, or incorrect liquid entropy.
The local-perturbation assumption can fail when long-range elastic interactions dominate the free-energy difference.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the special loss prevents collapse and supports the liquid state, whereas the mechanism describes the loss as penalizing the energy of liquid-like configurations. Taken literally, increasing the energy penalty on liquid-like configurations would destabilize rather than improve sampling of the liquid basin.
